correctness.rationale: For p,q>=2 with within-cluster distances s,t<=1 and cross distance one, a new point at distances R,U is metric exactly when 2R>=s,2U>=t,|R-U|<=1<=R+U. Write k=s(1-1/p), ell=t(1-1/q), both in (0,1). Positive invariant barycenter coefficients a,1-a have exact scalar Lipschitz extension norm max{1,[1-(1-k)a]/R,[ell+(1-ell)a]/U}, using distance-to-vertex scalar witnesses for equality and triangle inequality for arbitrary Banach upper bound. For the universal lower bound, extend the canonical isometric embedding of source vertices into the real Lipschitz-free space F(X). Any added vector is an affine combination of the source delta vectors; averaging over S_p×S_q in the convex norm envelope restricts without loss to one signed real parameter a. For a<0, concrete scalar 1-Lipschitz potentials force at least max{1,(1-a)/R,(1-a)ell/U}>=norm at a=0; for a>1 analogous potentials give >=max{1,ak/R,a/U}>=norm at a=1. Thus the global minimizer is nonnegative. The decreasing and increasing affine terms intersect at a0=(U-R ell)/(U(1-k)+R(1-ell)); clipping to [0,1] yields thresholds U=R ell and U=R/k, the three regimes and the exact norm-one interval condition. Independently checked all three strict regimes with exact fractions and signed out-of-range lower tests. The proof establishes the universal Banach quantifier, not just scalar extension.
residual_risks: The tested rational configurations do not prove the all-real all-size formula; the free-space convexity argument does. The new point need not make an ultrametric, but source must be two-cluster ultrametric.

value.rationale: An exact extension factor for every real Banach target is a meaningful intrinsic invariant of the simplest nontrivially hierarchical finite ultrametric sources. The three sharp support transitions and nonexpansive feasibility criterion distinguish cluster geometry that an equilateral-source formula misses, with use as a testbed for extension and free-space projection theory.
residual_risks: Only two homogeneous clusters and one new point; no claim for more clusters, quasi-Banach targets or multiple additions.

final_claim: The universal real Banach-valued one-point Lipschitz extension constant for a finite two-cluster ultrametric source has an exact three-regime formula with positive cluster barycenter optimizer and a sharp nonexpansivity boundary.
limitations: p,q>=2, 0<s,t<=1, real Banach targets and stated metric compatibility only.
